- **Screen shape**: `page.tsx` is a server component that reads with the person's session (`lib/member/context.ts`, `getMemberContext()`, cached per request: the session client, the firm with the person's role and function, `isSuperadmin`, currency and `org_entitlements`) and hands a `state` (`ready` | `error` | `unavailable`) to a client view that takes plain props. An error is never rendered as an empty state, and every write goes to the database function that owns the rule.
- **The gate of the logged area** (`app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx`, a server layout over `components/layout/dashboard-shell.tsx`; `lib/firm/gate.ts` reads, `lib/firm/gate-rules.ts` decides and is unit-tested): an account with no firm goes to `/auth/complete-profile`; the platform operator, who works in no firm, keeps `/admin` and `/settings`; whoever `second_factor_required()` names and has no verified factor goes to their own setup (`/configurar`, whose first step is the factor: the firm's for who manages it, the person's own for anybody else; 2026-11-03) and reaches nothing else, the platform operator to `/settings/security?exigido=1`; somebody of a partner of a firm (everybody of a partner owes the factor, 0069) is kept in the partner's area, sent instead to the partner's own setup (`/parceiro/configurar`, migration 0080, found through the registry's `partnerSetupOf` by the partner's kind), whose first step is the factor, and who manages a partner that never answered its setup finds it in place of the partner's home (an agency's first person sent to the security screen got lost there, the owner, 2026-11-03). The middleware writes the path into the `x-one-path` request header for it (`REQUEST_PATH_HEADER`), and stays query-free. It is guidance, not the fence: row-level security and `require_aal2()` in the functions are.
- **The firm and its team** (`lib/firm/roles.ts`, `lib/firm/actions.ts`, migration 0003): a membership says a role (`owner`, `admin`, `member`: the firm ACCOUNT) and a function (`socio`, `advogado`, `controladoria`, `atendimento`: the work). A person is in one firm at a time. Every change is a server action that calls the database function taking the firm; no rule is decided in TypeScript. An invitation link carries a random token whose SHA-256 is all the database stores; accepting takes an account whose CONFIRMED e-mail is the invited one. Without an e-mail provider the link comes back to the manager to send by hand. Colleagues read each other through `firm_team()`, never through `profiles`. A query on `memberships` always filters by `user_id`: a member reads every membership of their firm.
- **A module's share of the work** (migration 0078): the pages of the firm's work (`/casos`, `/atendimento`, `/aprovacoes`, `/protocolo`, `/publicacoes`, `/prazos`, `/agenda`) read every module of the firm, or one under `?modulo=<key>` (`pageScopeOf` and `scopedHref` of `lib/modules/offer.ts`; the choice is `components/product/module-scope.tsx`, above each page, and the crumbs pass through the module's area): the cases, deadlines and hearings by the database's own filter (`firm_cases`, `firm_deadlines`, `firm_hearings` with `target_module`), the packages and publications by their case, the conversations and the answers of the AI by `firm_module_conversations` and `firm_module_approvals` (a conversation is of a module when its contact is somebody of a case of it). What only a module has (its partner, its import, its test chat) is offered under that module and in its area, never on a page of every module. A page under a module keeps `modulo` in every link it builds, its pages and lists included.
- **The setup never leads away from itself** (the owner, 2026-10-30): `/configurar`, and the home while it asks the setup, holds nothing that takes the person out of a step before the firm is ready to work: no list of modules, no "see more", no link to another screen. Whatever a step needs is done in the step (the second factor, a model, a connection, an invitation: its link copied or sent by e-mail in place); what is information for later lives on the home or in its own page. A modules line with "Ver módulos" on the setup's first step took the owner out of a setup half done, and was taken off.
- **Nothing in a flow is met half way** (the owner, 2026-11-03): whatever a later step cannot be done without (the second factor, a role, a connection, a fact the database checks) is a step of its own before the first one that needs it, and the flow does not go past it until it is met. Before adding a step, list what each later step's writes ask for (the database's `require_aal2()`, a function's role check) and put each prerequisite in front. The second factor is the first step of `/configurar` (`SETUP_STEPS`, `setupOpening`): it was asked inside six steps, and the owner met it at the signer's switch of the first, before the registration at the bar.
- **ONE does the work; a person answers** (the owner, 2026-11-03): before a screen has a person do a task by hand (write, fill in, mark, copy, check against a rule), ask whether ONE's AI can do it from what the firm already has, and build that: the screen then shows what ONE did and that ONE may err, and asks only what only the person knows or decides (an answer, a choice of the firm's, a document to send again after a refusal said with why). How much ONE does alone is each firm's (`autonomy_decisions`, ONE by default). The first build of it is the firm's own model made from the document it already uses (migration 0079): sent in the setup's step or the library, refused with why when it cannot be one, the blanks asked in place (`biblioteca/import-panel.tsx`), and saved by ONE when nothing is left to look at (`saveGate` in `lib/library/imports.ts`).
- **A registration starts from documents** (the owner, 2026-11-03): a record a document already holds (a person, a trip) is made by sending the document (a photo, a PDF, a screenshot, a photo of a printed page) and confirming what ONE read, each field marked as read; typing is the contingency, offered as "Preencher à mão", never the first screen. The first build is the agency's (migration 0083): a new passenger starts as a draft traveler (`pax_start_traveler`: in no list nor count, swept after the setting's hours) that the documents sent to it name and fill, confirmed by the agency (`pax_confirm_traveler`), and a trip is read from its ticket, a booking's screenshot or a photo of a printed one (`pax_document_legs`), the document joining the trip once it is saved (`pax_attach_trip_documents`).
- **A card asks only for what is still owed, and says where each thing stands** (the owner, 2026-11-03): `CardTitle` leads every card a person works through with the icon of what it is and a `StatusChip` of where it stands; each thing it lists is a `StateLine` (done, waiting, attention, failed, info: an icon in the state's colour, the words saying it too); a request already fulfilled is said as done and doing it again is kept in `QuickActions`, one click away, while what is still owed, or arrived and does not serve, keeps its one button beside its line; an act the person must understand (an agreement given or taken back) is confirmed in an `OutcomeDialog`, never in an `Alert` at the top of the page. The first build is the passenger's link (`/acordo/[token]`, `agreement-view.tsx`, `documents-section.tsx`): the documents the firm needs (an identity of each person, a proof of address of the adult the link is for, `modules/direito-do-passageiro/agency/agreement-documents.ts`, pure and tested) ask in view only while they have not arrived or do not serve, "Enviar outro documento" holds another copy and the boarding passes, the card says when every one arrived, and agreeing opens "Acordo registrado" with the trips ONE follows, the WhatsApp the alerts go to, that the passenger decides whether they want help and how to leave.
- **The agency follows each flight as it happens; the firm foresees in numbers** (the owner, 2026-11-03; migration 0084): once a passenger agreed, `pax_flight_progress` gives the agency each followed trip's legs with when they left and arrived (as the source said, never from the clock), read by `modules/direito-do-passageiro/agency/flight-progress-actions.ts` and turned into steps by `flight-progress.ts` (pure, tested); `trip-flight.tsx` shows them under each trip of the passenger's page and `partner-flights-card.tsx` lists the next days' flights on the agency's home, as the module's `partnerHome` (a client component the core opens through the registry with `next/dynamic`, never by name), both read again every minute while a flight moves (`useFlightsRead`). The firm reads each partnership's `forecast` from `firm_partnership_facts` (`lib/partners/partner.ts`, `settings/parceiros/partnership-forecast.tsx`): counts by date, nobody named.
- A model of the library is also taken in Word where it is listed and written (`components/product/word-download-button.tsx`; `downloadWord` of `lib/library/word-download.ts` over `textDocx` of `lib/library/docx.ts`, which the library's reader reads back), with the marks as they are, so the file is the model.
- **Firm setup checklist** (`lib/onboarding.ts`, `@flyee/onboarding`, `components/product/onboarding-checklist*.tsx`): each step done when the thing exists in the database (`firm_setup_facts(org)`, migrations 0044 and 0056: a registration at the bar with somebody chosen to sign, a second person or an open invitation where the firm does not work alone, a connected number or the test chat; the Valor da Causa Pedido is chosen in the setup and never listed, since a firm that gives none lacks nothing, migration 0064; nor the first case, which a module brings and ONE opens, so the home says ONE waits for it while `first_case` is false, `waitsFirstCase`, and the list never makes it the firm's step, the owner's rule of 2026-11-03), never because somebody clicked, and each leads to its own step of `/configurar` (`?passo=`, `lib/firm/setup-steps.ts`), where it is done in place: the second factor it asks for, the models of the papers a client signs and the connections included. After them, a line per module the firm contracted whose own setup was never answered (`moduleSteps`, 0081). The home reads the facts under the person's session and mounts the card for who manages the firm; what a person keeps for themselves is only whether they dismissed it (`onboarding_state`).
- **Core and module setups are apart** (the owner, 2026-11-03; migration 0081): `/configurar` is the core, what every firm needs; what one module needs is that module's own setup, a page of its route group it declares in its definition (`firmSetup`, the registry's `firmSetupOf`; `lib/modules/module-setups.ts` and `module-setups-read.ts`), in the module's colour (`product_modules.tone`, `ModuleCard.tone`, `SetupWizard` `tone`), opened by the core's finish for each module the firm contracted and never answered, one after the other, then the home; a module not contracted is never set up, and its setup shows the others disabled (`QuickActionTile` with no `href`). A new module brings its setup in its own folder and touches nothing of the core's. The passenger module's is `configurar/(direito-do-passageiro)/direito-do-passageiro/`.
- **Each person's own setup** (`lib/firm/person-setup.ts`, `configurar/person-setup-view.tsx` and `person-setup-state.ts`): whoever joins a firm leaves their own work ready, the second factor first and, for a partner or a lawyer, the registration at the bar (the DJEN is read by it); on the home in place while something of it is owed and they never answered it (`onboarding_state`, flow `person-setup`), at `/configurar` for anybody who does not manage the firm; the firm's setup answers it for who manages it.
- **The menu by role** (`lib/firm/menu.ts`, unit-tested; `components/layout/viewer-context.tsx`): a menu item says who it is for (`canAccess`: the operator, an account with no firm, who manages the firm, some functions; nothing means anybody of a firm; a child inherits its group's), and the server layout hands the menus who is looking, so each person's menu is right on the first paint. The settings menu follows the same rule. It is guidance, like the gate: row-level security and the database functions decide what a person may read or do.
- **Entitlements**: `hooks/use-entitlements.ts` calls `org_entitlements(org)`, the single answer to what a firm may use. Screens branch on it, never on plan names. Limits are data on the plan rows: `assentos_max` is the seat ceiling the team screen shows and the invitation functions enforce. `components/product/gate-notice.tsx` renders the gate states; `components/layout/menu/plan-indicator.tsx` shows the tier.
- **Sign-up**: one person is one account, and `handle_new_user` creates the profile and nothing else. `/auth/callback` sends an account with no firm to `/auth/complete-profile` (or back to the invitation link it came from), where it accepts an invitation addressed to its confirmed e-mail (`my_firm_invitations()`) or founds a firm (`create_firm`) and becomes its owner. The campaign that brought a founder is attached to the firm at that moment (`lib/firm/actions.ts`), never at sign-up.
- **Usage events**: `lib/product-events.ts` (browser, only offers shown and clicked; it terminates the PostgREST builder with `.then()`, because a bare `void supabase.rpc(...)` never sends the request) and `lib/product-events-server.ts` (`trackServerEvent`, everything that counts toward a metric: `firm.created`, `invite.accepted`, the purchase events). The vocabulary and the allowlist of properties are in migration 0007: events, never content.
- **No tracker runs inside the logged area**: it shows client names and case numbers. The Pixel and GA4 exist on the public site only.
- Reusable blocks live in `components/product/*` and are listed in `components/product/catalog.json` (injected by the `product-screen-guard` hook). Every zero-data view uses `EmptyState`.

## Public site (marketing layer)

- Routes in `src/app/[locale]/(marketing)/`: home `/`, `/contato`, `/ajuda` and `/ajuda/[slug]`, `/blog` and `/blog/[slug]`, `/espera` and `/espera/confirmar`, `/descadastro`, `/legal/{termos,privacidade,cookies}`. It is a provisional ONE site (a home with three points, the waitlist and contact), to be rebuilt when the product has screens to show. A new public page is declared in `src/i18n/routing.ts` (that is also what makes it public to the middleware), enters `src/app/sitemap.ts` when indexed, and spreads `publicPageMetadata({ path, locale })` from `lib/seo.ts` into its `generateMetadata` (canonical and Open Graph URL; hreflang only if the site ever has a second language).
- ONE design system: pages compose the primitives in `src/components/marketing/` (`Section`/`Container`/`SectionHeader`, Hero, FeatureGrid, FeatureRows, RuledGrid, ProcessSteps, BentoGrid, StatBand, PricingSection, Faq, Cta), listed in `components/marketing/catalog.json`. `docs/DESIGN.md` describes the previous product's direction and is historical; until ONE commits its own, inherit what the components already do: no palette hue on small text, hues ride on icons, bars and fills.
- **No loading boundary above the public pages**: neither an `app/loading.tsx` nor a `<Suspense>` in the root layout. A boundary there starts the response before a page can call `notFound()` or `redirect()`, so a missing page answered 200 with `noindex` and a moved address got a meta refresh. Each signed-in area keeps its own boundary in its layout. The public 404 is `app/not-found.tsx` (marketing namespace, leads back to the site); the logged area has `app/(dashboard)/not-found.tsx`.
- **The loader overlay is for the signed-in areas only.** `#initial-loader` (root layout, `public/initial-loader.{css,js}`) covers the page until the window load event, while the shell settles. A public page arrives complete and styled, so the root layout leaves the overlay out (`isPublicPageRequest()` in `lib/public-page-request.ts`). Anything a public page decides in the browser and shows above the fold must be decided before the first paint, from `<head>` (the mode class), never after hydration.
- **Performance of the public site**: what a public page pays on a phone is the shared shell (MUI and its styling engine hydrate on every page, and one stylesheet carries the overrides of every dashboard component). Do not add to that cost: no scripted animation, no client component where a server one does, one icon import per icon.
- `/ajuda` and `/blog` render DB-managed content (written in `/admin/help` and `/admin/blog`) through `src/lib/public-content.ts` (anon client, published rows, in the language of the address); Markdown renders via `components/marketing/markdown-prose.tsx` (raw HTML ignored).
- **Legal pages render `consent_terms`** (`components/marketing/legal-document.tsx` over `lib/legal.ts`): the version in force of `terms`, `privacy` and `cookies`, with version and date, so the page shows exactly the text people accept. No legal document is seeded: until the operator publishes ONE's texts (`publish_consent_term()`), the pages say they have nothing to show. The catalog holds no second copy of the terms.
- **Launch stage** (`lib/launch.ts`, `platform_settings.launch`): in `waitlist` (the seed, and the fallback for anything unreadable) every primary CTA of the public site leads to `/espera`; in `open` they lead to sign-up. Sign-in and sign-up stay reachable in both. The superadmin flips it at `/admin/support`, which also holds the operating company printed in the footer (`legal_entity`, read by `getLegalEntity`).
- **Waitlist** (`/espera`): `espera/actions.ts` validates (honeypot, consent), calls `submit_lead` with the service role (first-touch campaign from the attribution cookie, network window keyed by an HMAC of the IP with `PUBLIC_FORMS_IP_SALT`), and e-mails the double opt-in link (`sendLeadConfirmationEmail`). The answer never reveals whether an address was already listed. The link `/espera/confirmar?t=` is rewritten by the middleware: the token moves into an httpOnly cookie (`COOKIE_KEYS.leadConfirm`) and the page loads at the clean address, because analytics scripts and Referer headers carry URLs; confirming takes a button press, because mail scanners open every link. `lib/lead-jobs.ts` runs `purge_expired_leads` daily (unconfirmed addresses go after 7 days, as the page promises).
- The contact form sends through `@flyee/email` (`CONTACT_FORM_TO`).
- Display type: `font-display text-display-{2xl,xl,lg,md}` (fluid clamp scale from `@flyee/design-tokens/css/marketing.css`). Motion: CSS first (the hero entrance in `style/layout/marketing-motion.css`, `<Float>`, the `<Reveal>` transition started by `watchEntry` in `components/marketing/motion.ts`); GSAP is loaded only by `<Parallax>`, on demand, and never in admin code. Transform + opacity, honors `prefers-reduced-motion`, nothing runs forever.
- **Site events** (`lib/site-events.ts`): four names (`section_view`, `cta_click`, `faq_open`, `contact_click`) as GA4 and Pixel custom events, declared on elements with `data-track` / `trackAttributes()` and on sections with `track="<key>"`, reported by the one listener in `components/consent/marketing-analytics.tsx`; never a third tracker. Add a name to the type and the set there before using it.
- **Tracking**: the marketing layout renders the Meta Pixel and GA4 server-side, behind one opt-out cookie and one notice (`lib/analytics.ts`). Sign-up, checkout and purchase conversions also go server-side (`lib/meta-capi.ts`, `lib/ga4-mp.ts`). The snippets are written once in `lib/tracker-snippets.ts`. Every key is blank in `.env.local` today, so nothing loads.

## Billing and checkout (the inherited ladder, rewritten in M3)

- `/settings/billing` (plans, current subscription, cancel with a reason and undo, invoices, billing profile, pending checkout, payment recovery) and `/assinatura?plan=<slug>` (the focused checkout: Pix, card or installments in BRL). Server actions in `settings/billing/actions.ts` (checkouts), `actions-cancel.ts` and `actions-recovery.ts`, sharing `billing-server.ts`; provider webhooks at `api/webhooks/[provider]/route.ts`, idempotent through `claim_billing_webhook_event`/`complete_billing_webhook_event` with an attempt ceiling.
- What M3 changes: Asaas and BRL only (Stripe, USD and the currency switch leave), tiers as data with ONE's limits (active cases, included AI, WhatsApp numbers), metering of active cases, a tier change on the live subscription. The one-time access ("kit"), the founders offer console and the entitlement keys of the previous product leave with it.
- What stays as it is: **dunning grace** (`past_due` keeps access for a configurable window, `billing_past_due_grace_ends()` is the one answer every gate shares); **comped plans** (`set_org_plan(org, plan, note)`, audited, refuses a provider-backed subscription); the guarantee window from `platform_settings` (`lib/guarantee.ts`); a pending PIX that survives a closed tab (`lib/pending-pix.ts`); **prices on screen** through `formatPrice` (`@flyee/billing/currency`: "R$ 97" when whole, "R$ 77,60" with cents), never struck through.
- ONE never moves case money: billing is the firm's own subscription and nothing else.

## Platform admin and account

- Superadmin area at `src/app/(dashboard)/admin`: `layout.tsx` is a server gate on `profiles.is_superadmin` (RLS stays the real defense); the Admin menu group renders only for the platform operator (`canAccess: { operator: true }`, `lib/firm/menu.ts`). Consoles: `/admin` (the counters of `admin_metrics()` and a tile per console), `/admin/escritorios` (firms), `/admin/leads`, `/admin/billing`, `/admin/ai` (cost per firm, per task and per model; the measure of each task, with the next version of its instructions and its autonomy written there; the categories of the AI's triage of publications, each let out of the shadow with a sample where it met the goal or put back, `components/triage-policy-card.tsx`; the executor check; the model price list), `/admin/calendario` (the forensic calendar every firm's deadlines are counted over: which years of each court were checked against the court's act, the days of a court and year, the acts of the list with their days; a change counts again the court's open deadlines whose count goes through the days it changed; `lib/admin/calendar.ts`), `/admin/audit` (audit trail + sign-in log), `/admin/backups`, `/admin/announcements`, `/admin/help`, `/admin/blog`, `/admin/support`.
- **Console shape**: `page.tsx` is a server component that reads through `lib/admin/*` inside `loadConsole()` (`lib/admin/session.ts`: the operator's session, `ready | error | unavailable`, so a failed read is never an empty list) and hands plain props to a client view; writes are server actions in the console's `actions.ts` that call `requireSuperadmin()` again (a server action is a public endpoint) and record an audit event; the database function that owns the rule is the one doing the write wherever one exists. Formatting is `lib/admin/format.ts` (pt-BR, Brasília clock, money per currency, never summed) and every database value becomes a word through `lib/admin/labels.ts`.
- **Firms** (`/admin/escritorios`, `admin_firms_overview()` / `admin_firm_dossier()` / `admin_people_without_firm()`, migration 0012): one row per firm; the tiles are the filters and count the same flags the rows carry (`lib/admin/firms.ts`). The dossier shows the ACCOUNT of a firm (team, invitations, what it may use, money, consents, sign-ins), never what the firm keeps in the product. The escalated actions act on a PERSON, from the menu of each person in the dossier or in the tab of accounts without a firm (`components/person-actions.tsx`): support access, reset 2FA, the superadmin role, ban and account deletion; ban, 2FA and deletion need `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`.
- **Leads** (`/admin/leads`): status tiles (confirmed, waiting, opted out), opt-out, erasure (`purge_lead`) and an export of confirmed, not opted-out contacts as a Resend contact CSV, audited. "Escrever para a lista" writes a message (Markdown), shows who would receive it before sending, and delivers it in batches (`newsletter_sends`, `lib/newsletter.ts`); a send that stopped is resumed from the same screen and never repeats a reader. Without an e-mail provider the screen says so and the button is off.
- Every mutation records an audit event through `lib/audit.ts` (`recordAudit`). Sign-ins are logged by a database trigger; people see their own in `/settings/security`.
- **Granting the superadmin role** (`set_user_superadmin(user, value, note)`): the flag is fenced by a trigger on `profiles` keyed on WHO is asking (`is_superadmin()` reads the database), because a self-`PATCH` of `is_superadmin` would otherwise promote any signed-in user. Self-change is refused in both directions. A session with no JWT (service role, migration, psql) passes: that is how the first superadmin is made.
- **Support impersonation** (`lib/impersonation-actions.ts`, started from `/admin/escritorios`, which a visit returns to): the operator works inside an account through a **parallel session cookie** (`@flyee/auth` `authCookieName`, marker `one-impersonating`), so leaving deletes a cookie and never strands the operator. Load-bearing: the write fence is in the DATABASE (`is_impersonated()` matches the JWT `session_id` against `impersonation_sessions`; triggers refuse writes to consent, the team tables and grants, and the team functions refuse it by name), and it never expires; ending a visit uses `signOut({ scope: "local" })`, never the global default; starting requires the operator's own session at AAL2; credentials and `/admin` are blocked in the middleware. A reason is required, the person is notified, and the access is labelled as support in their sign-in history. Duration lives in `platform_settings` (`impersonation`).
- **Account deletion** (`admin/escritorios/components/delete-account-dialog.tsx`, server action `deleteAccount`, RPC `admin_delete_account(user, confirm_email, reason)`): the unit is the person plus the firm they alone belong to; a person who is one of several in a firm is removed and the firm stays; the owner of a firm with other people in it is refused until the firm is handed over. The order is fixed: re-read the preview, cancel any live provider subscription (a failure deletes nothing), run the RPC in one transaction, then remove storage files through the Storage API using `admin_orphaned_account_storage`, which refuses anything still alive. Refused in the database: yourself, any superadmin, a support session, a live provider subscription. The audit event `admin.account.deleted` survives with counts only.
- **AI runs** (`lib/ai/*`, migration `0016_ai_runs`): a task goes through a model in one way, `runFirmTask(request)` in `lib/ai/executor.ts`, which wires the executor of `@flyee/ai/runs` to the database store (`lib/ai/run-store.ts`, the service role behind `start_ai_run` and `finish_ai_run`, never handed out). It records the run with its prompt version, the hash of the input, the answer and the cost, and puts the answer in the firm's queue when the task asks for a person. Never call a provider directly from a page, a route or a job: a call outside the executor is not recorded, not priced and not approved. `AI_FAKE_PROVIDER=1` makes the fake provider answer every task on a machine with no key (model name `fake`, ignored in production). `lib/ai/jobs.ts` gives up the runs nobody finished.
- **The vault** (`lib/connections/*`, migration `0017_connections`): `getVault()` is the one way to a firm's vendor token, for jobs and webhooks only. Open a token once per batch of work, naming the firm and a purpose (`vault.open({ orgId, connectionId }, "whatsapp.send")`): every open is audited, and a connection of another firm is not found. A page never opens a token, and a secret never goes into `connections.metadata`.
- **Files** (`lib/files/*`, migration `0018_files_documents`): `startUpload` (the person's session reserves, the backend mints the signed upload URL), `finishUpload` (the backend measures and keeps or rejects) and `downloadUrl` (a signed URL of a minute). The bytes never pass through a route of the app. Never read or write the `firm-files` bucket in another way.
- **Issued documents** (`lib/documents/*`): `issueFirmDocument(input, render)` is the one way a document is issued; the renderer prints the verification mark with `stampVerification`. `lib/documents/verification.ts` holds the pure rules of the public page.
- **WhatsApp** (`lib/whatsapp/*`, `@flyee/whatsapp`, migration `0019_whatsapp`): every delivery enters by one door, `handleDelivery(rawBody, signature)` in `lib/whatsapp/inbox.ts`, used by the webhook route and by the simulator alike: it tells whose signature the delivery carries (the vendor's app secret, or the simulator's own, which is drawn per process and never leaves it), parses, and `applyEvents` (`lib/whatsapp/events.ts`, pure and unit-tested) routes each event to its firm within that provider. A person's message goes out in two halves: `sendMessage` (`lib/whatsapp/actions.ts`) reserves it under the person's session, then `deliverOutbox` (`lib/whatsapp/send.ts`) claims and sends it and records what the vendor answered; `lib/whatsapp/jobs.ts` sweeps what was left behind and brings pending media into the firm's files (`lib/whatsapp/media.ts`). `providerFor` (`lib/whatsapp/provider.ts`) is the one way to a number's provider: it opens the firm's token from the vault for the work at hand. Never call the vendor, or write a `wa_*` table, in another way. An action has two halves, and only the person's is fenced by the database: before the backend's half does anything for a connection (open a token, call the vendor, record a simulated delivery) it asks the session the same two questions (`lib/whatsapp/session.ts`: not a support visit, the second factor confirmed). `WHATSAPP_SIMULATOR=1` turns on a number that exists only here (ignored in production). The vendor's browser SDK loads only on `/settings/connections`, and only after the person asks to connect: the logged area carries no third-party script otherwise.
- **AI spend** (price list at `/admin/ai`): every run that reached a provider records one `ai_spend` row, charged to the firm it was made for, written by the backend only, inside `finish_ai_run`. Prices are configuration (`platform_settings` key `ai_prices`, per million tokens), shipped empty; an unpriced model reports `priced = false`, and the console shows the unpriced count beside every total. Cost is stored in USD micros and converted only with an operator-set rate.
- `/admin/backups` (`@flyee/backup`): nightly from the clock's sweep (`lib/backup-jobs.ts`) plus "Run backup now" (inline). Archives land in the private `backups` bucket; downloads are signed URLs.
- Account plumbing is real: the header bell reads `notifications` (create rows server-side with `lib/notifications.ts`), announcements render in the dashboard layout with per-user dismissal, `/settings` edits the profile (avatar in the `avatars` bucket) and credentials. The quick-support widget (`components/support/support-widget.tsx`) reads the channels from `platform_settings` (`support`, edited at `/admin/support`), falls back to `BRAND.support`, and renders nothing until a human channel exists.

## Messages: bell, e-mail and scheduled jobs

- **Every message to a person is written in Portuguese**, by one copy object per channel: bell texts in `lib/messages/bell-copy.ts` (stored text, written by `notifyLocalized` in `lib/notifications.ts`), e-mail copy in `packages/email/src/copy/pt-BR.ts`. Both are typed so a second language would have to match the Portuguese object. Never write a sentence for a person at a call site.
- **A plan is called by `plans.name`**, never by a word in the copy. A date and an amount arrive already formatted for the reader (`lib/messages/format.ts`: the reader's time zone, `America/Sao_Paulo` when unknown).
- **Claim, then send.** A job that writes to people may run twice. The database marks the row in the statement that returns it (`claim_term_end_notices`, `claim_newsletter_batch`) and only then the message leaves. Where there is no row to mark, the bell's unique `source_key` is the fence (the welcome) and the e-mail goes only to who got a NEW bell row. A message may be lost to a failed send, never sent twice. A batch the provider refuses is given back (`settle_newsletter_batch`), so the next run tries it again.
- **Without `RESEND_API_KEY` nothing breaks**: senders return `{ sent: false }` with no error, the bell still rings, and a job does not claim what exists only as e-mail (a batch of the list). Without Inngest, what an action starts runs right after its answer (`startNewsletterDelivery`), the sweeps run while ONE is used, and nothing runs by the clock.
- **What a reader can stop**: the news (`profiles.marketing_email_opt_out`, the switch in `/settings`) and the messages to the list (`leads.opted_out_at`). Those carry `unsubscribeUrl(...)` in the body and as `List-Unsubscribe` (one click). `/api/public/email/unsubscribe` acts on POST only; a GET moves the request into an httpOnly cookie and lands on `/descadastro`, which asks with one button, because mail scanners open every link they deliver. Receipts and notices about the account ignore the preference.
- **Background work** (the owner's decision of 2026-11-04): the work a person's action leaves owed (a reading, a check, ONE's answer in a conversation, the next step of a case) is done right after their answer, on the same server, through `soon(label, task)` of `lib/jobs/soon.ts` (Next's `after()`; nested calls work), never through the job runner; each worker's `queue*` or `settle*` does it. What is left (a work that failed, one that waits for an hour of the day, the upkeep) is a **sweep** (`Sweep` of `lib/jobs/schedule.ts`: a key, when the clock runs it (every 5, 10, 15 or 30 minutes, at a minute of each hour, or a time of each day, UTC), whether it also runs while ONE is used, and its `run(service, until)`), declared beside the code it runs (`lib/*/jobs.ts`, `lib/*-jobs.ts`, a module's `jobs.ts` through `lib/modules/jobs.ts`) and listed in `lib/jobs/registry.ts`; a sweep missing from that list never runs. The job runner holds one function, the clock (`one-tick`, `lib/jobs/tick.ts`, listed in `app/api/inngest/route.ts`): a beat every five minutes that runs every sweep due at it in one step (`runSweeps` of `lib/jobs/sweeps.ts`: each on its own, a failure naming only the sweep, nothing started after the beat's time), about 18 thousand executions a month within Inngest's free 50 thousand. The sweeps that serve what people wait on also run while ONE is used (`whileUsed`), once in five minutes on each server, after the answer: `sweepWhileUsed()` of `lib/jobs/while-used.ts`, called by the logged area's layout, the pending center's read, the test chat's read, the client's link and the passenger's agreement link. A sweep claims each work in the database, so the clock, a round while ONE is used and a work after an answer never do anything twice; one that must never run from two servers at once (the DJEN, the tribunal's reading, ANAC's months, the backup, the newsletter) is the clock's only. A sweep's answer holds counts only. No event is sent to the runner.
- **Billing notices** go through `lib/billing-notices.ts` and never throw: by the time one runs the database is already right, and a webhook that failed on a bell would be replayed by the provider and reconcile the whole event again.
- **Auth e-mails** (confirmation, password recovery, e-mail change) are sent by Supabase, not by the app: `supabase/templates/*.html`. They are not rendered by any test here and still carry the previous product's texts: rewrite them with the ONE Supabase project.

## Auth

- Supabase through `@flyee/auth` (`client`/`server`/`middleware`/`service`). `src/middleware.ts` refreshes the session and protects everything except the public pages (`matchPublicPath`, from `src/i18n/routing.ts`) and `PUBLIC_PREFIXES`. Without `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`/`NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` the middleware no-ops and the auth screens show a configuration hint.
- 2FA (TOTP): enrolled at `/settings/security`; the middleware forces the AAL2 step-up at `/auth/two-factor`. M1 makes it mandatory by role.
- Internal redirects go through `lib/safe-next.ts` (`sanitizeInternalNext`), never a raw `next` parameter.

## Commands (run from the monorepo root)

- `npm run dev` — dev server. `npm run build` — production build. `npm run typecheck` — TypeScript 5.8 pinned to this app.
- `npm run test:web` — vitest. `npm run test:e2e` / `npm run test:a11y` — Playwright against a production build (`e2e/baseline.spec.ts`).
- `npm run lint:fix` / `npm run prettier` — lint and formatting.

## Watch out

- `src/style/global.css` imports tokens from `@flyee/design-tokens/css/*`; never recreate tokens locally.
- Deploys go ONLY through GitHub Actions (`.github/workflows/deploy.yml`, manual dispatch); the Vercel Git integration stays disconnected.
- Server-only secrets (`DATABASE_URL`, `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`, provider keys) never reach client components.
- `apps/web/.env.local` is a blank ONE file: fill a key only with an ONE development or sandbox credential (root `CLAUDE.md`, "Safety").
- After deleting a route, remove `apps/web/.next/types` before `npm run typecheck`: the generated route types of the last build still name it.

===== .claude/rules/app-ux.md =====

paths: ["apps/web/src/app/(dashboard)/**", "apps/web/src/components/product/**"]

# Product (authenticated app) UX

- The `product-screen` skill is MANDATORY for any create/edit here — a `PreToolUse` hook (`.claude/hooks/product-screen-guard.mjs`) loads it automatically; you never wait to be asked.
- **Goal, not table**: design from the user's job and what success looks like. Never default to a CRUD table of rows — that shape is allowed only when the job really is scan/compare/manage many rows.
- **Never a blank screen**: every zero-data view uses `EmptyState` (icon + why + the ONE next action). A brand-new user must find a path to value (the aha moment).
- **Less text on the screens, and no empty space** (the owner, 2026-11-09): a page, a card or a section opens on its title, and what it is for sits behind the "i" beside it (`description` of `PageHeader`, `CardTitle`, `CollapsibleCard` and `SectionTitle`; 200 characters at most, kept by `lib/i18n/hint-budget.test.ts`). `detail` keeps in sight only state or data (the kind of a case, a conversation's number, how many a list shows) and what must be read before acting (leaving the firm, what each decision of `/settings/autonomia` does, what a lawyer authorizes with the cloud signature, the release of a real passenger's alerts, and the instructions on the client's and the passenger's own pages). A row or a column that opens a list shows a chevron, never a sentence saying so; a definition that repeats its title goes; a tile is its icon and its name. A section with nothing in it takes a drawing of `@/icons/illustrations` (`EmptyState` `illustration`): the court with no lawsuit, the board with no case going, the goals with none, a module with no case, and every list with nothing in it (the cases, the conversations, the publications, the deadlines, the agenda, the filing queue, the library, the approvals, the operator's consoles); a state of permission or of a failed read keeps its icon. The owner found the controladoria, a module's area and the library tiring to read: 136 blocks of text under titles, about 2,800 words. The case screen had the same, card by card (2026-11-10): each card with nothing in it takes its drawing beside its words (the dossier's, in the narrow column, above them), a section inside a card says what it is behind the "i" of its sub-heading (`SectionTitle` `variant="subtitle2"` `as="h3"`: the suspension of the Tema 1.417, the acceptance of the civil court, the audios of the case, the preview of a piece), the way out of ONE's automation (a petition written outside, the reason a family goes together) sits behind an `InfoHint` beside its state line, and a state line drops the sentence that repeats the button beside it.
- **Onboarding never diverts attention**: a setup or onboarding screen (`/configurar`, the setup on the home, any `SetupWizard`) carries nothing that leads away from finishing it: no link to another screen, no "see more", no list of things to explore. Each step does its work in place (dialogs, inline forms, the second factor in the step); what is information for later lives on the home or its own page. A line of modules with "Ver módulos" on the first step of `/configurar` took the owner out of a setup half done (2026-10-30).
- **Prerequisites come first**: in a setup or any multi-step flow, whatever a later step cannot be done without (the second factor, a role, a connection, a fact the database checks) is its own step before the first step that needs it, and the flow does not advance past it until it is met. Never let a person reach a step and find it locked by something an earlier step could have settled. The second factor is the first step of `/configurar` for this reason (2026-11-03): it was asked inside six steps, and blocked the owner at the first.
- **ONE does the work, a person answers** (the owner, 2026-11-03): before a screen has a person do a task by hand, ask whether ONE's AI can do it from what the firm already has (read a document, fill a record from it, make a model of it, check it against a rule, ask for what is missing), and build that instead. The screen shows what ONE did and that ONE may err, and asks only what only the person knows or decides; a document ONE cannot use is refused with why and the way to send another. How much ONE does alone is each firm's (`autonomy_decisions`, ONE by default). The setup's step of the papers had no way to send the firm's own power of attorney: the firm sends the document it already uses, and ONE makes the model (migration 0079). The model keeps the firm's words (0093): only what changes per case becomes a mark, each field of the firm's form its own (`[[NOME]]`, `[[CPF]]`, `[[ENDERECO]]`), and the firm's society and lawyers stay as written once it says they are its own; the case says when a lawyer who signs is not among them.
- **ONE's work is never the person's task** (the owner, 2026-11-03): a checklist, a count, a pending line, an empty state or a message names as the person's only what a person does or decides. What ONE does by itself (opens a case from a module, sends a link, creates the lawsuits, writes a piece) is said as ONE's work, done, being done or waited for ("O ONE espera o primeiro caso"), never as a step the person owes, and a manual way to do it is offered as the exception it is, never as the primary action. "Abrir o primeiro caso" on the firm's setup list made a firm that had just finished its setup feel the work was manual, the opposite of what ONE is sold on.
- **A registration starts from documents** (the owner, 2026-11-03): where the record is already written on a document the person has (an identity, a proof of address, a ticket, a booking's screenshot, a photo of a printed page), the form opens on sending it; ONE reads it, fills the fields and marks each as read, and the person confirms or corrects what ONE read, being asked by hand only what no document gives. Typing every field is the contingency, offered as "Preencher à mão", never the first screen. The agency's new passenger was a form of typed fields while ONE already read the identity, the proof of address and the ticket on the passenger's page; it now starts from them (migration 0083).
- **A card asks only for what is still owed** (the owner, 2026-11-03): a request already fulfilled (a document that arrived and serves, a link already sent, an answer given) leaves the card's main area. The card says it as done (`StateLine` `done`, a green check; when nothing is left in the card, one line on its tint that says so: "Não precisa enviar de novo") and keeps doing it again one click away, in `QuickActions`. What is still owed, or arrived and does not serve, is its own line in the attention colour with its one button beside it. The passenger's link showed "Enviar identidade" to a passenger whose agency had already sent it.
- **Where things stand is said in icon and colour**: every card a person works through leads with the icon of what it is (`CardTitle`, its family's tint) and says where it stands in a `StatusChip`; each thing listed in it says its state in a `StateLine`: done in green with a check, under way in amber with a clock, to look at or act on in accent-3 with an exclamation, a failure in red (kept for failures), information in grey. The words always say the state too, never the colour alone.
- **An act the person must understand is confirmed in front of them**: what binds them or what others will act on (an agreement given or taken back, a decision) is confirmed in an `OutcomeDialog`: the state in a large icon, the title in their words ("Acordo registrado"), each consequence on its own line with its icon, one button ("Entendi"). A line of `Alert` at the top of the page is read past: the passenger who agreed on their link could not tell what they had agreed to start.
- **A check can be given, and a wait on the client has a way forward** (2026-11-04, migration 0094): what ONE read of a person waits for a look with "Conferi com o documento" beside it, and saving the person counts as that look (`confirm_person_read_fields`); a case whose account still lacks the client's answers says what ONE waits for and gives a partner or a lawyer "Seguir sem essas respostas" (`close_account_gaps`: the client is asked no more, ONE creates the lawsuits, the piece leaves those points to a lawyer); the client's "Terminei" says what they still owe of the account instead of "o escritório prepara a sua ação"; with no CPF lookup in the environment, the person shows no "CPF não consultado". The owner's test case sat with the piece never asked while the firm saved a person twice to "validate" it.
- **A paper a client signs is asked where it is owed** (phase 3, 2026-11-09, migration 0123): a bill in somebody else's name the firm accepts says under it, on the case's card of documents, who the holder is and who they are to the client, that ONE read the name and may have erred, and where the client's declaration of residence stands (the client's word, an address of another city a person looks at, ONE issuing it, the client signing it, signed); the client is asked on their link only who the holder is, and the declaration then comes to sign below; going on without it is a partner's or a lawyer's, with the second factor, a reason and what it may cost confirmed first. A name ONE read in capitals and the database wrote as a name is the same name: the line says a name was corrected only when its words changed, never its case or spacing.
- **The case says what happens now, and follows ONE by itself** (the owner's audit of the case screen, 2026-11-05, migration 0096): the top of `/casos/[id]` ("Andamento do caso", `journey-card.tsx` over `caseNow` of `lib/cases/now.ts`) says what ONE is doing at this moment, what holds the case and whose turn each thing is (the firm with the function that acts, the client, ONE, the platform of ONE), and what ONE did a moment ago, each line one click from its card; who has the case is computed from those lines, and every wait's owner comes from one table (`WAIT_PLACE` of `lib/cases/advance.ts`), which the center of what waits reads too. Another screen where ONE works on its record (an agency's passenger, a model being prepared) mounts the same notice over its own reading of ONE's work.
- **A page loads in its shape** (phase 0, 2026-11-07): every route of the logged area has a `loading.tsx` drawing `PageSkeleton` in the page's form (`list` for `/casos`, `/protocolo`, `/publicacoes`, `/prazos`, `/agenda`, `/biblioteca`, `/aprovacoes` and the agency's passengers, with the count of cards of numbers each has; `record` for a case and an agency's passenger; `home` for `/inicio`; `split` for `/atendimento`; `setup` for `/configurar` and the agency's setup; `cards` for every other page, `(dashboard)/loading.tsx`). The shell's fallback is the same skeleton, never the full-screen spinner over the menu it was. A new page gets its `loading.tsx` in its shape with it.
- **The menu's states float, and a group's page is a link beside its title** (the owner, 2026-11-07): "Em breve" and the lock of a module the firm did not contract float over the item's top edge at its right end (`CornerTag` `edge`; the owner, 2026-11-08), so "Direito Previdenciário" keeps its line; every submenu, for any kind of user, the operator's "Admin" included, closes once a page is reached and marks that page when opened again (the owner, 2026-11-08); the overview of the modules is "Todos" beside the submenu's title "Módulos" (`OverviewLink`; "Visão geral" beside "Admin"), never the item "Todos os módulos", which took a line and read as one more module.
- **Core and module setups are apart** (the owner, 2026-11-03): a setup asks what every firm needs in the core (`/configurar`) and what one module needs in that module's own setup, in the module's colour, after the core and before the home, only for the modules the firm contracted; the others are shown disabled, as what the firm could add. Never put a module's parameter in the core's setup, nor ask a firm to set up a module it does not have.
- **Everybody who joins has a setup of their own**: a firm's member, an agency's colleague; the second factor first, then what their function needs (a lawyer's registration at the bar), never a home with nothing said.
- Long setups use `SetupWizard` (progressive disclosure); steps to first result use `OnboardingChecklist` + `@flyee/onboarding` (state only; step definitions live in the project's code).
- **Engagement**: completion drive (`ActivationProgress`) and competence feedback only. Never ship points, badges, leaderboards or streaks — documented failures, and streaks carry regulatory risk.
- MUI v9 + theme tokens only, next-intl for every string, inline form errors near the field, skeletons that reserve space.
- **Semantic fields**: phone, CPF/CNPJ, CEP and money never go in a raw `TextField` — use `components/product/fields/*` (mask + check-digit validation + CEP auto-fill via `@flyee/fields`); persist `onlyDigits()`, never the masked string.

===== .claude/rules/design-tokens.md =====

---
paths: ["packages/design-tokens/**", "apps/web/src/style/**"]
---

# Design tokens

- `packages/design-tokens/css/*.css` is the source of truth for visual identity. `src/tokens.generated.ts` is GENERATED — never edit it manually.
- After any change in `css/*.css`, run `npm run tokens:generate` at the root and include the generated file in the same commit.
- Color values are bare HSL triplets (`191 100% 46%`), consumed via `hsl(var(--token))` in CSS. Keep this format; do not introduce hex/rgb.
- Every color token must exist in light/dark pairs (`:root`/`.dark` in common, `.theme-x`/`.theme-x.dark` in theme files).

===== .claude/rules/icons.md =====

---
paths: ["apps/web/src/icons/**", "apps/web/src/app/**"]
---

# Icon contract

- Pages import icons only as `@/icons/nexture/ni-*` (the alias may be remapped per project to an adapter set — see `apps/web/src/icons/README.md`). Never import an icon library (Phosphor, Lucide, MUI icons for decoration) directly in a page.
- Every icon component implements `NextureIconsProps` (`size`, `variant`, `className`, `oneTone`) and is a default export. The props type and the size helpers live in `src/icons/nexture-icons.ts`, which imports NO icon (every icon file imports it).
- `src/icons/icon-registry.tsx` (`IconMap`, `NextureIcons`) maps names to components and imports the whole set. Use it only where the icon name is data (the dashboard menu, a catalog icon typed by the operator); a client component that imports it ships every icon to the browser.
- Alternative sets live in sibling folders (`src/icons/phosphor/`, ...) with identical file names; gaps are filled by `npm run icons:stubs -w @flyee/web` (fallback re-exports, never overwritten).
- Adapters import icon libs from their SSR-safe entry (e.g. `@phosphor-icons/react/dist/ssr`) so they work in Server Components.

===== .claude/rules/marketing.md =====

# Marketing layer boundaries

> **State after M0 (2026-10-08).** The public site is a provisional ONE site in Portuguese: a home, the waitlist, contact, help, blog and the legal pages. The pages that sold flyee.club are gone. The `marketing-page` skill and `docs/DESIGN.md` were written for that product: their examples (the app store, the terminal, the founders offer, an English twin of every page) no longer apply, while the rules below do.

- **One design system.** Every public page composes the primitives in `apps/web/src/components/marketing/`: `Section`/`Container`/`SectionHeader` plus the archetypes listed in `catalog.json`. Never hand-tuned per-page spacing or widths, never a parallel stylesheet vocabulary.
- The `marketing-page` skill is MANDATORY for any create/edit/add-section under `app/[locale]/(marketing)`, `app/[locale]/(funil)` or `components/marketing`. The `PreToolUse` hook (`.claude/hooks/marketing-guard.mjs`) loads it automatically on Write/Edit in all three, and the `PostToolUse` lint (`.claude/hooks/marketing-lint.mjs`) checks every written file there. A file changed by a script bypasses both hooks: load the skill yourself and run the lint on it by hand.
- **Visual direction.** ONE has not committed its own direction yet: the palette (`theme-blue`), the logo and the type are provisional. Until it does, new pages and sections INHERIT what the components already do. Never restyle the UI or change the palette, the type or the logo unless the user explicitly asks. Adding a section triggers a whole-page coherence pass so all sections stay aesthetically aligned.
- **One language, in the path.** ONE is written in Portuguese only. Every public page lives under `app/[locale]/` in a folder named after its address, and is declared in `apps/web/src/i18n/routing.ts` (`pathnames`). That declaration is also what makes the middleware treat it as public: there is no separate list of public pages. Sign-in, the logged area, checkout and the admin have no locale in the URL.
- Internal links on public surfaces go through `LocaleLink` (`components/marketing/locale-link.tsx`, also as MUI's `LinkComponent`) or `localizeHref`: `href` is the internal path and the link renders the public address. Links to `/auth/*` and other non-public routes pass through unchanged.
- An INDEXED page also goes to `apps/web/src/app/sitemap.ts`. A `noindex` page (`/espera/confirmar`, `/descadastro`, any campaign page) stays out of the sitemap and is named in its exclusion comment. Indexing is decided by `metadata` + `sitemap.ts`, never by the route group.
- `/ajuda` and `/blog` are DB-managed: content is written in `/admin/help` / `/admin/blog` and fetched through `apps/web/src/lib/public-content.ts` (anon client, published rows). Content that could not be read is never shown as an empty list. Markdown renders via `components/marketing/markdown-prose.tsx`. Never interpolate DB content as raw HTML.
- SEO is part of every page: exactly one `<h1>` (the page title: `SectionHeader as="h1"` / `PricingSection headingAs="h1"` when the lead is not a `<Hero>`), a title + description via `generateMetadata` that spreads `publicPageMetadata({ path, locale })` from `lib/seo.ts` (canonical, Open Graph URL and locale), and structured data through `<JsonLd>` (`components/marketing/json-ld.tsx`), never a hand-written `<script>`. `Organization`/`FAQPage`/`Product` schemas are already emitted by the layout/`Faq`/`PricingSection`; do not duplicate them. Inner pages add `BreadcrumbJsonLd`. A missing page answers a real 404 and a moved one a real redirect: never put a loading boundary (`loading.tsx`, or a `<Suspense>` around the children of a layout) above a public page, because the response would start before `notFound()` or `redirect()` runs and go out as a 200.
- Marketing copy lives in the `marketing` namespace of `packages/content/messages/pt-BR.json`. No hardcoded strings.
- **Blocking on every public page**: exactly one `<h1>`, real `alt` text, no fabricated testimonials, metrics, logos or case results, prices and limits read from data (`plans`), no struck-through price and no "from/to" pair. Every number on a public page comes from the database.
- **What the site may say about the product.** ONE is software for law firms, sold by a technology company: it never promises the outcome of a lawsuit, an amount of compensation or a time to judgment, never speaks to passengers as if it were a law firm, and never says a step is automatic when a lawyer decides it (filing is assisted: the lawyer reviews and files with their own login).
- **What the site sells: ONE's core** (the owner, 2026-10-27). The copy is about the AI automation of a mass-litigation firm's cases: the client served on the firm's WhatsApp, the papers checked, the piece written, the deadlines counted, the filing package built, the firm choosing what a person reviews. It is never about an application built on it, such as the flight monitor that writes to passengers (Direito do Passageiro in `docs/PRODUCT.md`, the owner's "viagem segura"): a module is named at most in a line, as the first one, never in a title, the hero or the drawn screens.
- **Copy rules**: Portuguese, plain; no dash (— or –), no exclamation mark and no emoji in any visible text, `alt` and `aria-label` included (© and → stay, on purpose), and none of the banned words: desbloqueie, potencialize, sem esforço, soluções inovadoras. Where a dash would go, write a colon, a comma or a new sentence; separate items with "·"; a missing value hides its line instead of printing a placeholder. The rule covers the logged area, the e-mails, the bell and WhatsApp messages too; `lib/i18n/copy-rules.test.ts`, pgTAP `0033_copy_rules` and the e2e text check fail when a mark comes back.
- **Colour on text**: under the provisional palette no hue reaches 4.5:1 as small text on a light ground, so hues go on icons, bars and fills while the words keep text colours. The shared components follow it; a page must too.
- Motion is CSS first: the hero entrance and `Float` are CSS animations, `Reveal` is a CSS transition started by `watchEntry` (one shared IntersectionObserver in `components/marketing/motion.ts`), `CountUp` is a short frame loop. GSAP is loaded by `Parallax` alone, on demand. Never add a scripted timeline or a ScrollTrigger to a page, and never an animation without an end. Transform + opacity only, honoring `prefers-reduced-motion`. Never import GSAP in admin code.
- Site identity (name, tagline, siteUrl, favicons) comes from `apps/web/src/brand.ts`; the logo is the single component `components/logo/logo.tsx`.
- **Measurement is declared, never a new tracker.** A click worth measuring carries `data-track="<event>"` and `data-track-<prop>` attributes (or `trackAttributes()` from `lib/site-events.ts` on a link built in code), a section worth measuring passes `track="<key>"` to `Section` or the component that wraps one, and the one listener in `MarketingAnalytics` reports them to GA4 and the Pixel. The vocabulary is the type in `lib/site-events.ts` (`section_view`, `cta_click`, `faq_open`, `contact_click`): add to it there before using a new name. Never add PostHog or any other tracker, never write site events to the database, and never run a tracker inside the logged area or on a page a passenger opens by token.

===== .claude/rules/web-boundaries.md =====

# apps/web boundaries

- `apps/web` is the only app in this repo. Code shared between the app, the jobs and tooling lives in `packages/*`.
- Do not redefine theme tokens locally (`--primary`, `--grey-*` etc.) — they come from `@flyee/design-tokens`.
- This repo IS the ONE product: the platform for law firms (accounts, firms, cases, documents, courts, messaging, billing of the ONE subscription). Domain rules that decide something (forum, deadlines, prescription, eligibility) live in a package as pure functions with tests, never inside a page or a route handler.
- A page or route never talks to a vendor directly: it goes through the package adapter (real, fake, contract test), and through an RPC that receives the firm when it writes.
- The flyee.club surfaces (CLI delivery and OAuth, the module catalog, the club screens and consoles) are being removed in M0: do not build on them or extend them.
